technical-data.invention-title: CIRCUIT COMPRISING MEANS FOR REDUCING THE DC-OFFSET AND THE NOISE PRODUCED BY AN AMPLIFIER
CIRCUIT D'ATTENUATION DU DECALAGE EN CONTINU ET DU BRUIT PRODUIT PAR UN AMPLIFICATEUR

abstract.p: An amplifier (AMP) is provided with a pair of choppers (CHPi,CHPo) in order to reduce the DC-offset and the noise produced by the amplifier (AMP). To obtain an optimal noise reduction the pair of choppers (CHPi,CHPo) operate on a high frequency. As a result the DC-offset cancellation is not optimal because a so-called charge injection of the switches in the pair of choppers (CHPi,CHPo) produces a DC-offset. To overcome this problem the amplifier (AMP) is further provided with further offset cancellation means which are for example formed by a further pair of choppers (CHPfi,CHPfo). This further pair of choppers (CHPfi,CHPfo) operates on a relatively low frequency. The combination of the pair of choppers (CHPi,CHPo) and the further pair of choppers (CHPfi,CHPfo) guarantees an optimal DC-offset cancellation as well as an optimal noise cancellation.

La présente invention concerne un amplificateur (AMP)qui est équipé d'une paire de découpeurs (CHP1,CHPo) pour réduire le décalage en continu et le bruit que produit cet amplificateur (AMP). La recherche d'une réduction optimale du bruit explique que la paire de découpeurs fonctionnent sous une fréquence élevée (CHPi,CHPo). Par voie de conséquence, l'élimination du décalage en continu n'est pas optimale du fait que l'injection de charge des commutateurs dans la paire de découpeurs (CHPi,CHPo) produit un décalage en continu. Pour surmonter ce problème, on dote l'amplificateur (AMP) de moyens supplémentaires de suppression de décalage, par exemple sous forme d'une seconde paire de découpeurs (CHPfi,CHPfo). Cette seconde paire de découpeurs (CHPfi,CHPfo) fonctionne sous une fréquence relativement basse. La combinaison des deux paires de découpeurs (CHPi,CHPo) et (CHPfi,CHPfo) garantit une élimination du décalage en continu ainsi qu'une suppression optimale du bruit.

description.p: Circuit comprising means for reducing the DC-offset and the noise produced by an amplifier.

The invention relates to a circuit comprising an amplifier comprising an input for receiving an input signal from an input of the circuit, and an output for delivering an output signal to an output of the circuit; and means for reducing the DC-offset and the noise produced by the amplifier. Such a circuit is known from the general state of the art as shown in Figure 1.

The known circuit comprises an amplifier AMP having a differential input 5;6 comprising an input node 5 and an input node 6, and a differential output 7;8 comprising an output node 7 and an output node 8. The circuit further comprises an input chopper CHP, arranged in cascade in between a differential input 1;2 of the circuit and the differential input 5;6 of the amplifier AMP, and an output chopper CHP0 synchronised with the input chopper CHP,, which output chopper CHP0 is arranged in cascade in between the differential output 7;8 of the amplifier AMP and a differential output 3;4 of the circuit. The operation of the known circuit is as follows. An input signal V,n is supplied to the differential input 1;2. In response to the input signal Vιn an output signal Vout is delivered to the differential output 3;4. The input chopper CHP, is arranged for alternately coupling either input terminals 1 and 2 of the differential input 1;2 to respectively input nodes 5 and 6 of the differential input 5;6 during a first phase PHii, or input terminals 1 and 2 of the differential input 1;2 to respectively input nodes 6 and 5 of the differential input 5;6 during a second phase PHI2. The output chopper CHP0 is arranged for alternately coupling either output nodes 7 and 8 of the differential output 7;8 to respectively output terminals 3 and 4 of the differential output 3;4 during a first phase PHii, or output nodes 7 and 8 of the differential output 7;8 to respectively output terminals 4 and 3 of the differential output 3;4 during a second phase PHI2. The input signal V,n is converted to the output signal Vout in virtually the same manner as in the case that the input chopper CHP, and the output chopper CHP0 would not have been present. However by the presence of the input chopper CHP, and the output chopper CHP0 the offset produced by the amplifier AMP, which offset is denoted as Vos in Figure 1, is eliminated. Also the noise produced by the amplifier AMP is significantly reduced for frequencies lower than the switching frequency of the switches in the input chopper CHP, and the output chopper CHP0. For the purpose of reducing
the noise produced by the amplifier AMP the aforementioned switching frequency must be as high as possible.

A problem of the known circuit is that for a high switching frequency the so- called charge injection caused by the switches of the input chopper CHP, and the output chopper CHP0 causes a DC-offset in the output signal Vout. Thus with the known circuit an optimal DC-offset reduction can only be accomplished if the switching frequency is low. In that case the noise reduction is not optimal. On the other hand an optimal noise reduction is accomplished if the switching frequency is high. In that case however the DC-offset reduction is not optimal. Thus, with the known circuit, an optimal DC-offset reduction and an optimal noise reduction can not be accomplished at the same time.
It is an object of the invention to provide an improved circuit for reducing the noise and the offset of an amplifier.

To this end, according to the invention, the circuit of the type defined in the opening paragraph is characterized in that the circuit further comprises further means for further reducing the DC-offset produced by the amplifier.

The invention is based on the insight that the further means do not have to cope with the reduction of noise since the noise reduction is already optimally accomplished by the known circuit. In other words by the inventive circuit the problem of DC-offset reduction and the problem of noise reduction of the amplifier are uncoupled. The further means for further reducing the DC-offset produced by the amplifier may for instance comprise a further input chopper arranged in cascade in between the differential input of the circuit and the input chopper, and a further output chopper arranged in cascade in between the output chopper and the differential output of the circuit. The further output chopper is synchronised with the further input chopper. The switching frequency of the switches in the further input chopper and the further output chopper is significantly lower than the switching frequency of the switches in the input chopper and the output chopper.

The further means for further reducing the DC-offset produced by the amplifier may also be formed by other noise reduction systems. It may for example be formed in the manner as claimed in Claim 6. The invention will be described in more detail with reference to the accompanying drawings, in which:

Figure 1 is a circuit diagram of a known circuit for reducing the DC-offset and the noise of an amplifier;
Figure 2 is a circuit diagram of a first embodiment of a circuit according to the invention; and
Figure 3 is a circuit diagram of a second embodiment of a circuit according to the invention. In these Figures parts or elements having like functions or purposes bear the same reference symbols.

Figure 2 shows a circuit diagram of a first embodiment of a circuit according to the invention. The circuit comprises an amplifier AMP having input nodes 5 and 6 for receiving an input signal Vi„ which is available between input terminals 1 and 2 of the circuit, and output nodes 7 and 8 for delivering an output signal Vout to output terminals 3 and 4 of the circuit. For the purpose of reducing the DC-offset and the noise produced by the amplifier AMP the circuit is further provided with an input chopper CHPj, a further input chopper CHPf,, an output chopper CHP0, and a further output chopper CHPfo. The input chopper CHPj and the further input chopper CHPf, are cascaded in between the input terminals 1 and 2 and the input nodes 5 and 6, whereby the further input chopper CHPf, is cascaded in between the input terminals 1 and 2 and the input chopper CHP;. The output chopper CHP0 and the further output chopper CHPf0 are cascaded in between the output nodes 7 and 8 and the output terminals 3 and 4, whereby the further output chopper CHPf0 is cascaded in between the output chopper CHP0 and the output terminals 3 and 4. The operation of the circuit is as follows. The input chopper CHPi and the output chopper CHP0 receive a high frequency clock signal which is available between a first clock terminal CLKH and a reference terminal GND. By so doing the DC-offset and the noise produced by the amplifier AMP is significantly reduced. For obtaining an optimal noise reduction the frequency of the high frequency clock signal is as high as possible. In principle the DC-offset produced by the amplifier AMP would be virtually cancelled. However the so- called charge injections caused by the switches in the input chopper CHP; and the output chopper CHP0 cause a DC-offset at the output of the output chopper CHP0. To remove the DC-offset at the output of the output chopper CHP0 the further input chopper CHPf, and the further output chopper CHPf0 receive a low frequency clock signal which is available between a second clock terminal CLKL and the reference terminal GND. Because the further input chopper CHPfl and the further output chopper CHPf0 operate at a relatively low frequency the further input chopper CHPf, and the further output chopper CHPf0 do not introduce a DC- offset. The noise reduction of the further input chopper CHPf, and the further output chopper CHPfo is not optimal. This causes however no problem since the noise produced by the
amplifier AMP is already cancelled by the input chopper CHP; and the output chopper CHP0.

Thus the combination of the input chopper CHPj, the output chopper CHP0, the further input chopper CHPf, and the further output chopper CHPfo guarantee an optimal DC-offset reduction and also an optimal noise reduction of the amplifier AMP. It is to be stated that though the frequency of the low frequency clock signal must be relatively low, it must not be chosen unnecessary low since the maximum transfer frequency of the circuit is in practice limited to half the value of the low frequency clock signal.

Figure 3 shows a circuit diagram of a second embodiment of a circuit according to the invention. An important difference with respect to the first embodiment is that the circuit does not comprise the further input chopper CHPfi and the further output chopper

CHPfo. The cancellation of the DC-offset at the output of the output chopper CHP0 is carried out in a different manner. This has the advantageous effect that the maximum transfer frequency of the circuit is much higher. The circuit is provided with a switch SW connected in between the input terminals 1 and 2. A control electrode of the switch SW is connected to a control terminal STyp- The circuit further comprises an analog to digital converter ADC with an input connected to the output terminal 3, and with an output; a digital processing circuit DPC with an input connected to the output of the analog to digital converter ADC, and an output; and a digital to analog converter DAC with an input connected to the output of the digital processing circuit DPC, and an output coupled to the amplifier AMP. The operation of the circuit is as follows. At the start-up of the circuit the inputs of the input chopper CHPj is short-circuited under control of a start-up signal Vsτ which is available between the control terminal STIJP and the reference terminal GND. The DC-offset at the output of the output chopper CHP0 is measured and fed back to the amplifier AMP in order to adapt the DC-offset of the amplifier AMP. This measurement is in fact accomplished by sampling the signal at the output of the output chopper CHP0 during the start-up of the circuit. The sampling is accomplished in the digital domain in order to avoid the problem of leakage of a necessary sampling capacitor in the case that the sampling would be accomplished in the analog domain. For this reason the analog to digital converter ADC converts the analog output signal Vout to a digital representation of the analog output signal Vout- The digital sampling is then performed by the digital processing circuit DPC. The digital output signal delivered by the digital processing circuit DPC is then converted to an analog signal by the digital to analog converter DAC for adapting the DC-offset of the amplifier AMP. The feedback loop created by the analog to digital converter ADC, the digital processing circuit DPC and the digital to analog converter DAC is active until the DC-offset at the output 3;4 of the circuit is virtually
zero. Then the start-up signal VST switches off the switch SW and the circuit is then ready for transferring the input signal V-,n to the output signal Vout. The adaption of the DC-offset of the amplifier AMP can for instance be accomplished by controlling a current of one transistor of a differential input pair within the amplifier AMP. By way of example the differential signal from the output chopper CHP0 is transferred to a single-ended output signal Vout by a further amplifier AMPf.

If the circuit does not have to operate continuously the "start-up procedure" can be repeated now and then, for instance by doing a re-calibration after each sampling performed in the digital domain. This has the advantage that a potential DC-offset due to a temperature change after the completion of the start-up, is avoided.

Though varies signals are indicated as differential signals with regard to the first and the second embodiments the invention can also be carried out with single-ended signals. So for instance in Figure 2 the input terminal 2 and/or the output terminal 4 could also be connected to the reference terminal GND. The inventive circuit can be implemented with discrete components as well as with an integrated circuit. All types of transistors can be used.

claim.claim-text: 1. A circuit comprising an amplifier (AMP) comprising an input (5;6) for receiving an input signal (V,n) from an input (1;2) of the circuit, and an output (7;8) for delivering an output signal (Vout) to an output (3;4) of the circuit; and means for reducing the DC-offset and the noise produced by the amplifier (AMP), characterised in that the circuit further comprises further means for further reducing the DC-offset produced by the amplifier (AMP).

2. A circuit as claimed in claim 1, characterised in that the means for reducing the DC-offset and the noise produced by the amplifier (AMP) comprises an input chopper (CHPj) arranged in cascade in between the input (1;2) of the circuit and the input (5;6) of the amplifier (AMP), and an output chopper (CHP0) synchronised with the input chopper (CHP;), which output chopper (CHP0) is arranged in cascade in between the output (7;8) of the amplifier (AMP) and the output of the circuit (3;4).

3. A circuit as claimed in claim 2, characterised in that the further means for further reducing the DC-offset produced by the amplifier (AMP) comprises a further input chopper (CHPf,) arranged in cascade in between the input (1;2) of the circuit and the input chopper (CHP,); and a further output chopper (CHPfo) synchronised with the further input chopper (CHPf,), which further output chopper (CHPf0) is arranged in cascade in between the output chopper (CHP0) and the output (3;4) of the circuit.

4. A circuit as claimed in claim 3, characterised in that the input chopper (CHP;) and the output chopper (CHP0) are operative as high frequency choppers, and that the further input chopper (CHPf,) and the further output chopper (CHPf0) are arranged as low frequency choppers.

5. A circuit as claimed in claim 1 or 2, characterised in that the further means for further reducing the DC-offset produced by the amplifier (AMP) comprises switching means (SW) for short-circuiting the input signal (V,n) under control of a start-up signal (VSτ); and
means for feeding back a sampled output signal to the amplifier AMP for adapting the DC- offset of the amplifier.

6. A circuit as claimed in claim 5, characterised in that the means for feeding back the sampled output signal comprises an analog to digital converter (ADC) with an input coupled to the output (3;4) of the circuit, and with an output; a digital processing circuit (DPC) with an input coupled to the output of the analog to digital converter (ADC), and an output; and a digital to analog converter (DAC) with an input coupled to the output of the digital processing circuit (DPC), and an output coupled to the amplifier (AMP) for adapting the DC- offset of the amplifier (AMP).
